requests.question: OI-20260831-TRADE-PRIORITISATION-IS-LIVE-BUT-UNPROVEN-AND-ITS-AB-HARNESS-DOES-NOT-EXIST is a `loud` row whose clears_when has three clauses. (2) and (3) are met in full and its own text says a NULL closes it. Clause (1) says "scripts/backtest_system.py grows an N-book mode", and the capability was built as a parity-asserted SIBLING instead, for the landing-surface reason in `deviation_from_done_condition`. Should the row be removed?

options.label: Reword clause (1) to name the CAPABILITY, then remove the row
options.implication: Makes the next reader's test the one that matters - does the capability exist and is it drift-proof - rather than which file it lives in, and then closes an answered question. RECOMMENDED.

options.label: Remove the row as it stands
options.implication: The register stops carrying an answered question. Correct if the substance is what clears_when meant. The evidence is committed and the write-up is linked from the design file, so nothing is lost by removal.

options.label: Keep it open until scripts/backtest_system.py itself carries the mode
options.implication: Reads the clause literally. Costs an open `loud` row that every session must report on while the question behind it is answered - the alarm-fatigue shape this repo treats as its own P1.

requests.context: The row is left OPEN with a full `observation` recording exactly what was built, measured and deviated from, so whoever decides is deciding on the evidence rather than on a summary. Removing a `loud` row is a judgement about a deviation from a written condition, and a sub-session that cannot put the deviation to anyone should not make it silently.

requests.question: The exit-eval 60s promise is breached on 6.2% of restarts (20 of 325 post-fix, max 210.4s) and on 14 within-process intervals in 18 days. Both causes are now named. Two exact Tier-2 remedies are ready, independent of each other, each with a one-env-flip rollback. Which, if any, should be armed - and is the restart boundary in scope for the 60s promise at all?

options.label: Arm R2 only - the per-pass IB circuit breaker
options.implication: The larger effect on the larger live residual. Once one IB fetch returns a pinned-thread queue timeout, skip the remaining IB packages in THAT pass. Changes NOTHING about what any package receives - a skipped package gets the same candles=None it would have got 29s later - it bounds the cost of an outcome already determined. Pass cost in the reset window falls from n x 29s to ~35s. Rollback EXIT_LOOP_IB_BREAKER_DISABLED. Cost: during a transient (non-outage) queue timeout, later IB packages are skipped for one pass and retried 30s later.

options.label: Arm R2 and R1
options.implication: R1 additionally moves _start_exit_loop above _apply_per_account_leverage in src/main.py::main() - measured 2.0-10.0s off the startup term, median ~3s, and it is the 10s tail it targets. Must stay AFTER boot_reconcile so a pass cannot evaluate a journal row the reconciler is about to void. Rollback EXIT_LOOP_EARLY_START_DISABLED. Cost: the cold first pass then overlaps the leverage pre-flight on a 2-core box.

options.label: Arm R1 only
options.implication: Touches only startup ordering and no fetch behaviour - the smaller blast radius of the two - but it addresses the persistent 6.2% restart-gap tail and leaves the reset-window residual entirely.

options.label: Record a DECIDED on whether the restart boundary is in scope, and arm nothing
options.implication: A legitimate answer. The restart gap is 19-60s by construction, so keeping the 60s promise across a restart means changing one of the four measured terms - there is no version of the current design that comfortably clears it. If the boundary is declared out of scope, that must be RECORDED with its consequence stated (756 s/day unevaluated), never left looking like a fix about to happen.

requests.context: MEASURED 2026-09-10T06:13Z from GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak (whole-file summary + breached_only=true&limit=2000, both COMPLETE censuses: 1218 of 1218 breach rows, 444 of 444 measured boundaries), plus four /api/diag/journalctl restart windows and a 1000-row /api/diag/log_file tail. RESTART GAP: min 17.5s, median 40.5s, p90 56.0s, p95 60.9s post-fix; it decomposes as residual cadence sleep 0-30s + systemd downtime ~0.3s + startup-to-thread 6-15s + cold first pass 12.7-16.9s, reconciling exactly on all four measured boundaries - i.e. 19-60s BY CONSTRUCTION against a 60s requirement, with essentially no headroom, at 18.1 restarts/day. Total exposure 756 s/day (12.6 min/day, 0.875% of wall clock) in which no open position's exit is evaluated - and 93.8% of that is from COMPLIANT restarts, so the breach rate understates it. WITHIN-PROCESS: 97.0% of the 1218 predate 2026-08-22; the live residual is 14 breaches in 18 days, 10 of them in the 04:00-05:00Z IBKR reset window, where each IB-routed package pays a serialized 29.0s pinned-thread queue timeout so a pass costs n_IB_packages x 29s and crosses 60s at THREE packages.
requests.objectTitle: The exit-eval 60s breaches have TWO different causes - a closed within-process episode plus a live IBKR-reset-window residual, and a structural restart gap with no headroom
